Name: Gadget Valley
Author: moomeowmeme
Description:
[size=6][b]Gadget Valley[/b][/size]
[i]Catch the lightning. Charge the batteries. Build the gadgets.[/i]

Your lightning rods have been filling up with Battery Packs all along. Gadget Valley gives you something to build with them: [b]twelve battery-powered gadgets[/b] for the mines, the river and the farm. There's a Ladder Finder, a Fish Finder that shows what's biting, a Machine Scanner, Rocket Boots, a Grow Lamp, a Power Strip that speeds up your kegs, a Hive Heater for winter honey and more. Every recipe is known from the start. The Battery Packs are what you'll have to work for.

[line]

[size=5][b]In your hands[/b][/size]
Hold a gadget and [b]right-click[/b] to use it, the way you'd use a totem. Right-clicking something you can already use (a door, a chest, an animal, a ripe crop, a machine, a ladder in the mines) still does that, so you can harvest with the Crop Scanner in hand.

[b]Ladder Finder[/b]
If a ladder or shaft is already on the mine floor, a bobbing "Ladder!" tag marks it and a message says which way and how far ("A ladder, 14 tiles to the northeast"). That's always free. If there's no ladder yet, it uses one Battery Pack to charge, and the next rock you break opens a way down. The charge keeps until you use it, even across floors, and it isn't spent on a floor that already has a way down, so it won't make the Staircase pointless. On monster floors it tells you the way down opens when every monster is gone.

[b]Fish Finder[/b]
Stand at the water's edge facing the water and right-click. A window lists [b]every fish that can bite at that spot right now[/b]: this season, this weather, this time of day, at your fishing level, the same way the game picks a fish when you cast. It knows the mines' floors too. Fish you've never caught are faded; point at one to see its name. It leaves out legendaries you've already caught, and what only a crab pot catches.

[b]Crop Scanner[/b]
While you hold it, every crop on screen gets a small tag: [b]"Ready"[/b] or the days left ("3d"), garden pots included, counting a Grow Lamp's extra growth. Crops that still need water today get a reddish tag. Right-click for a summary: "24 crops in sight: 6 ready, 3 need water."

[b]Machine Scanner[/b]
The Crop Scanner for machines. While you hold it, every machine on screen gets a tag: [b]"Ready"[/b], [b]"Empty"[/b], the time it'll be done today ("4:30 pm") or the days left ("2d"), counting a Power Strip's speed. Kegs, jars, furnaces, bee houses, tappers, casks (days to iridium) and crab pots ("Bait" when one needs it) all count. Right-click for a summary: "18 machines in sight: 5 ready, 9 working, 4 empty."

[b]Metal Detector[/b]
While you hold it, it beeps, faster the closer you get to an artifact spot or seed spot, and a [b]signal meter[/b] over your head fills from green to red. It's silent when there's nothing within 25 tiles. Right-click to mark the nearest spot with a "Dig!" tag.

[b]Home Remote[/b]
One press and you're home, just inside your front door (your own cabin in co-op). It's used up like a Warp Totem, and one recipe makes three. It doesn't work at festivals or while swimming.

[line]

[size=5][b]Wear them[/b][/size]
These two have the battery built in. Each one works for [b]a whole season (28 days)[/b], counted from the first time you put it on. A message tells you when it switches on, and again each morning of its last three days. When the battery runs out, it turns into a gray [b]Spent[/b] version (ordinary boots, or just a hat), and you craft a fresh one.

[list]
[*][b]Rocket Boots:[/b] +1 speed, like coffee that never wears off.[/*]
[*][b]Headlamp:[/b] a hat that lights up the area around you, like the Glow Ring.[/*]
[/list]
[line]

[size=5][b]Set them down[/b][/size]

[b]Grow Lamp[/b]
A lamp you place among your crops. Each night, every [b]watered[/b] crop within 2 tiles gets an extra day of growth, so stages, regrowth and giant crops all work as normal. Overlapping lamps still give one extra day, not one each. It lights up at night like a lamp-post.

[b]Power Strip[/b]
Set it among your machines. Every machine within 2 tiles [b]works faster[/b], finishing in about three quarters of the time: a week of wine in a little over five days. It works on kegs, jars, furnaces, crystalariums and the rest, and casks age faster too, reaching iridium in about three quarters of the time. Overlapping strips don't stack.

[b]Hive Heater[/b]
Bee houses within 3 tiles [b]keep making honey all winter[/b]: wild honey (there are no flowers) every 4 days. Honey that's still being made when fall ends carries on into winter. It glows at night too. The rest of the year it does nothing, and bee houses work as usual.

[b]Pond Aerator[/b]
Set it right next to a fish pond, touching its edge. That pond's fish [b]multiply twice as fast[/b], and on a morning when the pond has nothing to collect, it gets a second chance at making roe or something else, at the pond's own odds.

[line]

[size=5][b]Where the power comes from[/b][/size]
Every gadget is built with the game's own [b]Battery Packs[/b], which you get from lightning rods (Foraging level 6) and solar panels. For more lightning, there's a [b]Storm Totem[/b] (1 Battery Pack, 1 Oak Resin, 40 Wood): use it and tomorrow brings a thunderstorm with far more lightning than usual (before a festival, the storm comes the day after). On a day whose weather the game has already decided, such as the first of the month or the Night Market, it tells you so and isn't used up. If you also use my mod [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/54099]PackRat[/url] (1.1 or later), which has the same Storm Totem, you'll only see one, PackRat's; keep PackRat up to date so the two match. Totems you've already made carry over between the two.

[size=5][b]Recipes[/b][/size]
All known from the start, in the crafting menu.
[list]
[*][b]Ladder Finder:[/b] 1 Battery Pack, 3 Iron Bars, 1 Gold Bar[/*]
[*][b]Fish Finder:[/b] 1 Battery Pack, 2 Iron Bars, 2 Refined Quartz[/*]
[*][b]Crop Scanner:[/b] 1 Battery Pack, 2 Copper Bars, 2 Refined Quartz[/*]
[*][b]Metal Detector:[/b] 1 Battery Pack, 2 Iron Bars, 1 Gold Bar[/*]
[*][b]Machine Scanner:[/b] 1 Battery Pack, 2 Iron Bars, 2 Refined Quartz[/*]
[*][b]Home Remote (makes 3):[/b] 1 Battery Pack, 1 Copper Bar, 1 Refined Quartz[/*]
[*][b]Rocket Boots:[/b] 3 Battery Packs, 2 Iron Bars, 10 Coal[/*]
[*][b]Headlamp:[/b] 2 Battery Packs, 1 Iron Bar, 2 Refined Quartz[/*]
[*][b]Grow Lamp:[/b] 2 Battery Packs, 1 Gold Bar, 3 Refined Quartz[/*]
[*][b]Power Strip:[/b] 3 Battery Packs, 2 Iron Bars, 1 Gold Bar[/*]
[*][b]Hive Heater:[/b] 2 Battery Packs, 3 Copper Bars, 5 Coal[/*]
[*][b]Pond Aerator:[/b] 2 Battery Packs, 2 Iron Bars, 1 Refined Quartz[/*]
[*][b]Storm Totem:[/b] 1 Battery Pack, 1 Oak Resin, 40 Wood[/*]
[/list]
[line]

[size=5][b]Install[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*]Install [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/2400]SMAPI[/url] (4.1 or later).[/*]
[*]Unzip Gadget Valley into your [b]Stardew Valley/Mods[/b] folder.[/*]
[*]Run the game through SMAPI.[/*]
[/list]Needs Stardew Valley 1.6.9 or later. No other mods needed.

[b]Removing it:[/b] gadgets in your world turn into Error Items if you uninstall, so sell or trash them first.

[size=5][b]Compatibility[/b][/size]
Gadget Valley adds its items and recipes through SMAPI's content API and doesn't patch the game's code, so it should get along with most mods.

Downloads.Description: Unzip into your Stardew Valley/Mods folder and launch the game through SMAPI.

Manifest.Name: Gadget Valley
Manifest.Description: Twelve battery-powered gadgets built from Battery Packs: a Ladder Finder, a Fish Finder, a Machine Scanner, Rocket Boots, a Grow Lamp, a Power Strip, a Hive Heater and more. Plus a Storm Totem, for more lightning.
